en: Regarding the *Shōryūji Ki* (Record of Shōryūji) concerning the preliminary yoga: one should always abide in the visualization of the principal deity (*honzon*). When walking, one should practice the visualization of treading upon lotus flowers.
Next, upon reaching the gate of the shrine, snap the fingers three times while reciting "HŪṂ," and gaze with the right eye.
Visualize the syllable *ma* in the left eye and the syllable *ṭha*; with *ma* as the sun and *ṭha* as the moon, enter the doorway and look back. This accomplishes five benefits:
namely, (1) the joy of all Buddhas, (2) the removal of defilements, (3) the manifestation of radiance, (4) the expulsion [of obstructors], and (5) the sealing of the boundary.

Next, form a vajra-fist with the left hand at the heart and extend the wind-wheel (index finger); do the same with the right hand, rotating them to the left and right above the crown of the head, pointing toward the upper direction and the lower realm while reciting the mantra of the syllable HŪṂ.
Next, perform three circumambulations and pay homage to the Buddha.
Next, set forth the words of repentance, beginning with "From past lives... and so forth.
Next, take your seat and again pay homage to the Buddha.

Next, to purify the three karmas, join the palms with an open heart and add the syllable *ĀḤ* (*𑖠*) to the four locations of the three-karma mudrā; this is used together with the armor-binding (*kavaca*) of the three families.
Next, empower the scented water and sprinkle it for purification using the three-pronged mudrā (*triśūla-mudrā*).
Next, perform the recitation of the *devatā-vibhāga*.

Next, offer a prayer for protection with a mind of reverence, saying "The Buddhas of the ten directions and three periods of time," and so forth, according to the instructions in the ritual manual (*vidhi*).
Next, perform the Awakening Buddha Seal and the Fire-Wheel Seal, which are the same as those in the Vajradhātu.
Next, chant the ninefold prostrations according to the text; if the mind is distracted, recite Mahāyāna sūtras.
Next, perform the four immeasurables as usual.
Next, for the mantra of the supreme mind, employ the vajra-pañjali mudrā.
Next is the Vajra-wheel as usual;
next is the earth element;
next is the boundary of the four directions.
Next, one should sit according to what is appropriate for the body. Within the mind, one visualizes the initial syllable *ĀḤ* surrounded by nine concentric circles of empty space, white in color.
Then, one enters the Buddha-samaya-mudrā, touching the forehead, right shoulder, left shoulder, heart, and throat, and circling the face three times.
Next, perform the Fire-Wheel Seal of the Arising of the Dharma-Dhātu according to the ritual procedure.

Next, perform the Wind-Wheel Seal of the Turning of the Wheel of Dharma; apply the seal three times clockwise to the five locations on the forehead, visualizing the turning of the Wheel of Dharma throughout the three thousandfold world system.

Next, having donned the armor and formed the mudrā, visualize the syllable Oṃ at the right shoulder (1), the back of the neck (1), the forehead (3), and the back of the head (3); then form the gesture of binding the hair above the right and left ears.

Next, one dwells in meditative absorption and contemplates the "Crest Jewel" (Uṣṇīṣa-maṇi); placing the bright white syllable *ra* upon the crown of the head, sinful defilements are eliminated and merit and wisdom are brought to perfection.

Next, perform the mudrā and mantra of the Able-to-Bear (Akṣobhya): with palms joined hollowly, extend the two water-fingers (ring fingers), rotate them three times both upward and downward, and empower the four places.
Next, perform the mudrā and mantra for rousing the Earth Goddess according to the ritual procedure.
Next, the Earth Goddess holds [the vessel].
Recite the mantras in sequence according to the ritual procedure.
Next, perform the mantra for the altar and empower the altar by performing the Tathāgata-fist mudrā three times.
Next, perform the mantra and mudrā for sprinkling purification according to the ritual manual.
Next, recite the verse for the Earth Deity (*pṛthivī-devatā*) while holding the incense burner, chanting: "The compassion of all Buddhas," and so forth.
Next, perform the *bhadra-mudrā* (alms-bowl mudrā) for inviting the Earth Deity, and perform three beckoning gestures with the words "Vāyu" (Wind).
Next, perform the mantra and mudrā of Dharaṇīdhara according to the ritual procedure.

Then, in the Karuṇāsambhava Maṇḍala, sit in the full lotus posture (paryaṅka) and, at a distance of one cubit in front [of you], visualize the syllable *HŪṂ* upon a white lotus. With the fire of wisdom (*jñānāgni*), burn away all afflictions (*kleśa*) so that both the sentient beings and the vessel-world (*bhājanaloka*) are completely purified.
Next, establish the five syllables.
Next, visualize the syllable *Aṃ* (𑖮) at the crown of the head, which is the hundred-fold pervasive illumination.
Next, place the phrase of non-arising (*A*) at the heart.
Next, visualize the syllable 𑖿 (ra) on the surface of the chest.
Next, establish the stainless eyes, meaning the two eyes gaze upon the syllable 𑖿.

Next, perform the fire-wheel mudrā, place it at the heart, and rotate it three times; next, perform the upward-facing mudrā, rotate it three times in the sky, and then release the mudrā from the body.

Next, perform the Earth Wheel Mudrā; recite the mantra and place it between the two knees. For earth, water, fire, wind, and space, place them respectively in their appropriate positions: the water mudrā is in front and faces downward; the fire and wind mudrās are in front and face upward; the forms of the mudrās are as usual.
Next, place the vajra-pañjali mudrā at the heart and recite the five-syllable mantra of fulfillment.
Next, establish the vessel-world (bhājana-loka); visualize the wheel of space (ākāśa-cakra) situated in the lower realm, its dimensions being immeasurable.
The mudrās for wind, fire, and water function in sequence with their tips all pointing downward.

Next, abiding in the *samādhi-mudrā*, one visualizes that upon the earth-wheel (*pṛthivī-cakra*) the syllable *vaṃ* forms an ocean; within the ocean, the syllable *aṃ* forms a five-pronged wisdom-vajra; above that, the syllable *hoḥ* forms the *karma-vajra*; and above the *karma-vajra*, the syllable *hrīḥ* forms an eight-petaled lotus, with the two nāga kings Nanda and Upananda supporting the lotus on its left and right.
Next, the mantra of Mahāsāgarāmudrā is according to the ritual procedure.
Next, the Vajrapāṇi holds a flower with the five-pronged inner-binding mudrā.
Next, the Great Mantra King employs the karma-mudrā.
Next, the eight-petaled lotus seal is placed upon the five-wheeled mudrā (*pañcakula-mudrā*).
Next is the lion-throne seal, which is to be orally transmitted with the addition of the mantra *ājñāpayati āḥ jvale*.

Then, upon the lotus pedestal, the syllable *āḥ* transforms into a vast palace terrace, its steps fully composed of the seven precious jewels; one should visualize it according to the ritual procedure.
Next is the mantra of Ākāśagarbha.
Next is the seal of the Great Wheel Maṇḍala, which is the seal of the Small Vajra Wheel.
Next are the seals for spreading the various colors and for the boundary lines; outside, one binds the five garments with their seed-syllables, and so forth.
White, red, yellow, blue, and black, respectively; faith, diligence, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom—these are explained in detail as before.
Then, reciting the seed-syllables of the five colors, one performs the fivefold rotation of the mudrās to manifest the five colors, emerging from within to the outside in their respective order.
Next, recite *Namo samantabuddhānāṃ* and *Hūṃ*. With another rotation, it becomes the vajra-womb boundary (*vajramaṇḍala*).
Then, abiding in the mudrā of meditative concentration, visualize the seed-syllables of all the deities within the central womb clearly and distinctly arranged.

First, visualize the Great Enlightened One’s Lion Throne and the eight-petaled lotus; upon the throne is a pure moon disc of universal radiance, within which the long syllable *HŪṂ* is placed. This transforms into Mahāvairocana Munī, pure and free from all defilements, his wondrous form transcending the three realms, and so forth.

Surrounded by the retinue of the eight-petaled maṇḍala, within the moon discs of the eight petals are the syllables *a*, *ā*, *u*, and *ū*, which transform into the Buddhas Ratnaketu, Saṃkusumitarājendra, Amitābha, and Dundubhisvara.

Within pure moon disks at the four corners are the syllables *Aṃ*, *Āṃ*, *Mum*, and *Yūṃ*. These transform into Samantabhadra, Mañjuśrī, Avalokiteśvara, and Maitreya, adorned with their respective forms, colors, facial expressions, hand gestures (*mudrā*), and insignia (*cihna*), all in accordance with the ritual manual.
Each seed-syllable, each honored form, each physical characteristic, and each samaya should be visualized according to the ritual method without omission.
If one is unable to do so, visualize the syllable *vaṃ* at the center of the mandala; it emits golden light that universally illuminates the three tiers of the courtyard.
The letter *A* transforms into the various deities, and the seed-syllables transform into their respective forms and characteristics.
Contemplating them in this manner, one finds that this realm contains thirteen assemblies.

Regarding the statement, "The body in meditative equipoise within the pure moon-disc of universal light is surrounded by the retinues of the eight maṇḍalas," this precisely clarifies the central treasury (*garbha*) of the mandala.
Next, the seal of Samantabhadra in the east is called the second assembly;
Avalokiteśvara in the north constitutes the third assembly;
and Vajrapāṇi placed in the south is what is known as the fourth assembly.
In the direction of Nairṛti, Akṣobhya Tathāgata acts as the messenger; in the direction of Vāyu, Vijaya-trailokya is the fifth assembly.
The four great guardians of the four directions shall constitute the sixth assembly.
The first gate, Śākyamuni, is precisely the seventh assembly;
the third, Mañjuśrī, should be the eighth assembly;
and the southern one, Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, constitutes the ninth assembly.
The Vidyottama section concerning Kṣitigarbha is called the tenth assembly;
the section concerning Ākāśagarbha in the northern direction is the eleventh assembly;
and the Susiddhi section concerning the retinue is the twelfth assembly.
The World-Protecting Deity of Majestic Virtue is called the Thirteenth Assembly.
This is the first of the sequential distributions.
Next, place the five [syllables] outside the jewel-crown and the raised hand-gesture upon the crown and forehead; recite the five types of *ā* for bestowing life-force.
Next, for the Armor Mudrā, divide the forehead into three sections and take refuge three times for each.

Recite the twenty-eight syllables beginning with *Ka* while slowly circling toward the back of the head, the throat, and the heart center, respectively, visualizing them accordingly. For the eighty-four *akṣaras* beginning with *Ka*, *Kha*, and *Ga*, all employ the aforementioned mudrā.
Next, with the thirty-six [syllables] beginning with *I*, perform the previous mudrā around the navel.
Next, place the Universal Mudrā at the chest and recite the two wheels of the expedient means—namely, the two types of wheels—adding thirty-four [syllables] to each nose-tip to form the body-light.
Next is the mandala of the Lotus-Vajra family and others, which, like the Buddha-family mandala, consists of three layers of maṇḍalas located upon the body, and so forth.
Next, one arranges the seed-syllables and mudrās of concentration, distributing the thirty-two distinct syllables.
Next, place the seal of Samantabhadra at the heart and recite the four kinds of mantras: the Bodhicitta-samādhi, the Bodhicaryā-prajñā-janana, the Bodhipratiṣṭhāna-pūrakaraṇa, and the Śānti-nirvāṇa.
Next, abiding in the mudrā of meditative concentration, one contemplates the inner maṇḍala as described in the original record.
Next is the Great King of Mantras, the Contemplation of the Equality of the Dharmadhātu; therein one arranges twelve syllables, which correspond likewise to the twelve links of dependent origination.
Next are the eight secret mudrās;
next is the Wisdom-of-Wisdom mudrā of Fulfillment;
next is the oral instruction on "reaching nowhere."
Next, for the Hundred-Light Universal Illumination, one forms the seal of meditative absorption and arranges the seed-syllables; as the text says, "universally sealing," and so forth.
Next, for the Heart-Mantra of all Buddhas, one uses the Vajra-Palm Seal.
Next, for Uruvilvā-Kāśyapa and Gayā-Kāśyapa, one uses the Brahma-Casket Seal; these are the mantras of the Śrāvakas.
Next is the consort Ākāśalocanā. Next is the Mother of Seven Koṭis of Buddhas;

her mudrā consists of the hands of wisdom and means interlaced within, with the two fire fingers (index fingers) held upright and joined at their tips, the wind fingers (middle fingers) placed against the upper joints of the fire fingers, and the space fingers (thumbs) each resting against the side of the wind fingers.
The mantra is: *Namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvānāṃ tadyathā oṃ jvala su-jvala jvālāmukhi svāhā*. Next is the Bodhisattva Mahāvīra, who uses the Universal Mudrā; the mantra is as follows:
*Namo samantabuddhānām āryamahāvīra svāhā.* Next, the general mudrā and mantra of Mahāsukha-vajrasattva are as follows:
*Namo samantabuddhānām vajrayogasaṃvara satvaṃ.* Next is the general mudrā of all Bodhisattvas.
Next is the mudrā of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva;
next, the mudrā of Tārā Bodhisattva;
and next, the mudrā of Bhṛkuṭī.
Next is the seal of Mahāsthāmaprāpta; next, the seal of Yaśodharā;
next, the seal of Sitātapatrā.
Next is the seal of Hayagrīva.
Next are the seals taught by all the bodhisattvas, which are universal seals; the mantras follow below.
Next is Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva.
Next is the general seal of all those who follow the teachings;
next is the seal of Vajrapāṇi; next is Māmakī.
Next is the Vajrasūcī; next is the Vajraśaṅkara mudrā;
next is the wrathful Candramukha.
Next is the earth-holding mudrā of all Vajradharas;
next, the vajra-fist; next, all Vajradharas.
Next is the Bodhisattva Prajñāpāramitā;
next is Acala Vidyārāja;
next is the five-pronged [vajra] within the seal of the Victorious One of the Three Times.
Next, the mudrā and mantra of Trailokyavijaya are as usual.
Next, the root mudrā of the Great Majestic Wisdom King (Mahātejas-vidyārāja) is as usual.
Finally, the four great protectors are positioned below.
Next is the seal of Śākyamuni from the first gate;
next is the seal of Prajñāpāramitā;
next is the seal of the ūrṇā-kośa.
Next, the Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣa according to the ritual procedure;
next, the Sitātapatrā-uṣṇīṣa according to the ritual procedure;
next, the Vijayoṣṇīṣa.
Next is the mudrā of the Most Victorious Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa;
next is the mudrā of the Light-Cluster Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa;
next is the mudrā of the Abandoning Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa.
Next is the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa mudrā of Viśvabhū;
next is the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa mudrā of Saṃbhava;
next is the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa mudrā of Anantaghoṣa.
Next is the Brahmakośamudrā for the assembly of śrāvakas;
next, the assembly of pratyekabuddhas;
next, the Aparājitāmudrā.
Next is the seal of the secondary consort.
Next is the seal of Mañjuśrī according to the ritual manual.
Next is the Bodhisattva Jālinīprabha.
Next is the Vimalaprabhā-mudrā; next is Kīṭasani; next is Upakīṭasani.
Next was the Bodhisattva Bhūmimati;
next, the youth Citra; next, the youth Āhvayana.
Next, the five who receive the instructions are all named Acintya-kumāra.
Next, perform the seal of Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin in the south according to the ritual manual.
Next, perform the seal of Vimati-cchedaka.
Next is the Bodhisattva Bestower of Fearlessness;
next, the Remover of Evil Destinies;
next, the Bodhisattva Protector and Benefactor.
Next was the Bodhisattva Mahāmaitrījanman;
next, Karuṇādānārdrā;
next, the Bodhisattva Tāpanāpahārin.
Next is Acintyamatī; next is the Honored One Kṣitigarbha of the Supreme Direction;
next is the Bodhisattva Ratnākara.
Next was the Bodhisattva Ratnapāṇi;
next, the Bodhisattva Dharaṇīdhara;
next, the Bodhisattva Ratnamudrāhasta.
Next is the Bodhisattva Dṛḍhamati;
next, in the direction of the nāgas, is Gaganagañja;
and to the left of Gaganagañja is the Bodhisattva Dānapāramitā.
Next is the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīla-pāramitā*).
Next is the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*).
Next is the perfection of diligence (*vīrya-pāramitā*).
Next is the Dhyāna-pāramitā.
Next, to the right of Gaganagañja, is the Prajñā-pāramitā.
Next is the Upāya-pāramitā.
Next is the perfection of aspiration;
next is the perfection of power;
next is the perfection of wisdom.
Next is Gaganāmala, next is Gaganamati,
and next is Padmamudrā Bodhisattva.
Next is the wisdom of purity;
next is the wisdom of practice;
next is the wisdom of abiding.
Next appears the Bodhisattva Sūkṣmasiddhi-jñāna;
next is the Bodhisattva Pañcākāśagarbha holding a lotus-vajra.
Homage to Vajrasvāhā; next is the mudrā of Īśvara.
Next is the seal of the Sahāmpati deva;
next, the Ābhāsvara deva;
next, the Manasvin deva.
Next is the Heaven of Universal Sound;
next is the Heaven of Īśāna;
next are the Sarvārthasiddhas.
Next is Śakra of the East;
next is the seal of Dhṛtarāṣṭra;
next is the Sun Deity.
Next is Mārīcī. Next is Sūrya, the Lord of the Day, the consort of the Sun; her mantra is:
*Namaḥ mahāgātapataye svāhā*. Next are the Nine Planets (*Navagraha*).
Next is the Brahmā seal;
next is the consort seal;
next is the gandharva seal.
Next were the asuras; next, the mahoragas; next, the kinnaras.
Next was Agni; next after him, Vasiṣṭha.
Next was the seer Ārṣṭiṣeṇa;
next was the seer Gautama;
next was the seer Gārgya.
Next is the Southern King Virūḍhaka;
next is the Seal of the Staff (daṇḍa-mudrā) of King Yama;
next is the King of Death.
Next is the seal of the Seven Mothers of Yama;
next, the Night Goddess;
next, the Queen of Yama.
Next is the Officer Who Carries Out the Teachings;
next, the Ḍākinīs; next, the King of the Garuḍas.
Next is King Tiriṭi in the southwest; next, the rākṣasīs;
next, leading his elder brother Puyin, Jāṅgulī, Kālakarnī, svāhā.
Next were the hosts of rākṣasas;
next was the Heavenly King Virūpākṣa of the western quarter;
and next was Varuṇa.
Next, Nanda and Upananda;
next, the various nāgas;
next, the earth deities.
Next is the deity Ghoṣa;
next, Nārāyaṇa; and finally, the last.
Next, [offerings] to Vināyaka;
next, to the Moon Deity;
next, to the twenty-eight lunar mansions.
Next is the Heavenly King Maheśvara;
next is his consort Umā;
next is the Wind Deity of the Vāyu direction.
Next is Vaiśravaṇa in the north;
next are the yakṣas; and next are the yakṣiṇīs.
Next, all the piśācas; next, all the piśācīs;
next, all human beings.
Next, invite the devas; next, the Universal Illuminator Queen (Viśvaprabhā-vidyārājñī);
next, the two guardians for each gate, the inviolable protectors.
Next, face one another and provide protection.
Next, perform purification.
Next, perform the mudrā of the Immovable Sword to expel obstructors and establish the boundary, sealing the five places of the body.
Next, [perform] the mudrās of the hook, the noose, the chain, and the bell.
Next, establish the body with the *garuḍa-jvālā-prāṇāgni-cakra-mudrā*.
Next, again, with the sword mudrā, dispel those following Māra; this is the binding of the *daśadig-rakṣā-ārya-acala-mudrā-mantra*.
Next, enter the Buddha-samaya;
next, the Ākāśajāla;
next, the Fire Enclosure.
Next, ring the bell.

Holding the ritual hammer (mudgara) in the right hand, place it at the waist; holding the bell in the left hand, place it at the waist without producing sound, and ring the bell slowly. With the hands positioned at the waist facing outward, place one's own tongue in the mouth.
Next, draw and cast the *vajra* three times to expel obstructors and establish the boundary; seal the five places, and then settle the mind in composure.
Next, hold the bell at the shoulder and beside the ear, and ring it five times.
Next, shake [the bell] twice each over the chest and the forehead.
Next, strike the five places of the body with the *vajra* seal, and then return it to its original position.
Next, the praise of the four wisdoms.
Next is the argha conch seal;
next is the flower seat;
next, Akṣobhya indicates the seat.
Next, the mudrā of concentration;
next, donning the armor;
next, terrifying Māra.
Next is the great boundary (mahā-sīmā).
Next are the four great guardians of the four directions—northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest—in accordance with the ritual procedure.
Next are the two guardian mudrās for each of the gates.
Next is the seal of Acala’s sword;
next, the incense;
next, the flower-garland seal.
Next, burn incense;
next, offer food and drink;
next, provide lamps and light.
Next is the Vidyārājñī of Ākāśagarbha.
Next, the expanded verse beginning with "By the power of my merit," and so forth.
Next is the brief praise of the heart-mantra.
Next, prostrate to the Buddha.
Next, express gratitude with the words "Various incenses and flowers," and so forth.
Next, the Samaya: Born from the Dharmadhātu, the Sattva.
Next is the Great Wisdom Sword;
next, the Dharma Conch;
next, the Vajra Seat.
Next is the Vajramahāprajñā mudrā;
next is the Mahātathāgatoṣṇīṣa; next is the Tathāgatanimitta.
Next, the Ūrṇā-kośa (Hair-tuft) mudrā.

Next, for the Tathāgata’s nose: form the *baddha-puṭa* (closed-fist) and open the palms; with the sides of the wind-fingers (*vāyu-aṅguli*) acting as supports, press the lower joints of the wind-fingers against the void.
The mantra for the nose is:
Homage to Oṃ riṇi hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.
Next, the great bowl mudrā;
next, the gesture of granting fearlessness.
Next is the Wish-Granting [Mantra].
Next is the Tathāgata’s Lasso [Mantra].
Next is the Tathāgata’s Heart [Mantra].
Next, the navel of the Tathāgata;
next, the waist of the Tathāgata;
next, the secret organ of the Tathāgata.
Next, Universal Radiance;
next, Tathāgata Armor;
next, Tathāgata Tongue.
Next is the Tathāgata’s speech;
next is the Tathāgata’s teeth;
next is the Tathāgata’s eloquent exposition.
Next, the ten powers of the Tathāgata;
next, the foundations of mindfulness of the Tathāgata;
next, the discourse on impartiality.
Next is Samantabhadra-maṇi; next, Maitreya;
next, the Vidyārājñī Unobstructed Power.
Next, [recite] the *vidyā* of the Consort Invincible Power (*Anantavīrya*). Next, consecrate the rosary.

Next, place the root mudrā with its five clouds at the heart and so forth; visualize oneself as identical to the deity, and recite the root mantra over the four places: the crown of the head (*oṃ*), the chest (*vama*), the two eyes (*huṃ*), and the heart (*e*).
Next, hold the water-filled vessel and the jewel two inches apart; facing the forehead, make a vow and recite the mantra according to the ritual.
Upon completion, place the jewel back in its original position.
Next, perform the mudrā of stabilization and contemplate the five syllables—ĀḤ, VAṂ, MAṂ, HŪṂ, and TRAṂ—in both reverse and forward order as requested.
Next, upon emerging from meditative absorption, bind the root mudrā and recite the root mantra seven times to empower the four places.
Next is the Ākāśanetra mudrā.
Next is the Universal Mudrā placed at the heart, which says:
"By means of these merits thus maintained, entrust them to the Mother of the Family; until the time of attaining Buddhahood, may she protect and mind them so they are not lost.
Next are the seals of the five offerings.
Next, briefly praise with the *Cittānandaka-gāthā*.
Next, [recite] the *Ākāśagarbha-vidyārājñī*.
Next, ring the bell.
Next, perform the arghya offering and make the aspiration prayer.
Next, perform the empowerment with the Universal Seal (Samantamudrā) and seal the five places [of the body].
Next, recite the second mantra for releasing the boundary by circling counter-clockwise from the "Unbearable" (Duṣprasaha).

Next, for the Immovable One, the Buddha-samaya, the enclosure wall, the net of space, the flames, and the earth-binding, all are released by circling counter-clockwise; however, for the earth-binding alone, one simply extracts it.
Next, place the vajra-palms at the heart and recite the invocation beginning with "All Tathāgatas present before me," and so forth.
Then, escort the Bhagavān outside with the fire-wheel seal (*vahnimaṇḍala-bandha*). Finally, holding a flower above the crown of the head, cast it onto the maṇḍala with a solemn and resonant voice.
Next, perform the three secret protections as before.
Next, place the vajra-palms upon the crown of the head and recite the homage syllable *Oṃ*.
Next, place the fire-wheel mudrā at the heart and recite the homage syllable *Hūṃ*.
Next, place the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa mudrā at the heart and recite the syllable *Aṃ*.
Next, place the vajra-palms at the heart and say:
"Whosoever hears my voice, Or sees me, or touches me,"
The mind is the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha;
all its merits are equal to those of the World-Honored One Vairocana,
without any distinction.
Next, one contemplates the syllable *aṃ* within the heart.
The syllable *vaṃ*, with its great dot of emptiness (*bindu*), is the gate of liberation of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha*).
The syllable *haṃ* is detached from causes and conditions; it is the gate of liberation of signlessness (*animitta-vimokṣamukha*).
The visualization of the syllable *Uṃ* through samādhi is the door of liberation of wishlessness (*apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha*).
By relying on this contemplation of liberation, one is able to eliminate the obstacles to practice.
Thereafter, one exits the maṇḍala and accords with the points of training (*śikṣāpada*).
Copied from the original manuscript kept at Hachiman-ji in the first year of Keian (1648).
Proofread once by the śramaṇa Eihan.
Jōgen, age thirty-nine. Copied on the intercalary fifth month of the first year of Tenmei (1781), the year of Chou, from a manuscript preserved at Eshin-in, Uji. Jinin.
In the eighth month of autumn during the Kenwa era, I obtained the original manuscript and transcribed it.

With a compassionate heart, I had the Imperial Court’s *Denpōroku* (Record of the Transmission of the Lamp) and other texts collated and punctuated with national characters (*kokuji*). I further verified and edited them before carving them onto woodblocks, so that the Dharma may be transmitted.
Recorded by Kaidō of Sōji-in, residing at Myōon in Chōkō, Fusen-zan.
